newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares ebb but scoops up turnover.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares ebb but scoops up turnover.

text.p: Egyptian share prices continued to ebb in the Cairo stock market on Monday, but brokers say they see the decline as short-lived and expect an upturn.
The all-share index shed 10.39 points to end at 357.69 in 39.45 million pounds ($11.6 million) worth of turnover, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) said.

"There's volume so that means somebody is buying. I think local institutions are selling because they want to take their profits and show it on their books," said Dalia Sultan of EFG/Hermes. "I don't think this (fall) should continue further than this week. People want to buy but they are waiting to see the bottom of it."

"The prices are going down very rapidly. The good news is that we're getting closer to where we are going to see a lot of money coming into the market again," said Mohammed Abdullah, Intercapital managing director.

"The reason was that we overreacted since the prices were up in January and February. This is typical of an emerging market, which is going between extremes, and we'll see a lot of foreign money coming back in the market."
Share prices have mostly fallen since the 1997 high in February of 423.09 points.
Commercial International Bank (CIB) continued to fall, losing 3.26 pounds to close at 70. But its turnover was the highest in the day at 6.76 million pounds.
For the second day, a housing share shone. Medinet Nasr Housing and Development shares rose the highest, up 9.9 pounds to close at 470 in just over 1 million pounds trade.
"For Medinet Nasr to go up on a day like this is very, very significant," said Abdullah. "The housing sector has been gaining confidence in general and Medinet Nasr is a very strong company."
Housing shares have been faring well recently. But Heliopolis Housing and Development fell 12 pounds to 403 with stock worth 1.1 million pounds traded.
Kabo/Nasr Clothing and Textiles ended up 4.56 pounds at 95.67 in trade worth 3.4 million pounds.
"This is not a very liquid stock to start with. The government had announced it would privatise Kabo so maybe people are starting to take chances in the stock," Abdullah said.
General Silos and Storage trade was worth 2.78 million pounds, but it fell by 3.2 pounds to 99.8.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 504.89 points and the rarely-traded "closed" firms fell to 260.49 from 265.42.
Out of the 83 shares traded, 12 ended up, 51 fell and 20 were unchanged
